summary: Re-tested FINAL bug #1 after main agent removed clearDraft() COMPLETELY from success.tsx.goNext(). BUG STILL 100% REPRODUCIBLE. Tap testID=success-continue → URL flips to /transfer/new within ~300 ms and stays there through T+8000 ms. Same console error as iter_5/iter_6: 'Cannot update a component (ForwardRef(NavigationContainerInner)) while rendering a different component (TransferStep2 ./transfer/details.tsx)'. The clearDraft hypothesis from iter_5/iter_6 is INVALIDATED — clearDraft is no longer called, draft is non-null throughout, yet details.tsx still triggers the redirect-to-/transfer/new during its render. The root cause is the broken Rules-of-Hooks structure in details.tsx (useEffect placed AFTER an early return, with eslint-disable to silence the rule). React still treats the previously-registered effect as live and synchronously re-runs setState (router.replace) inside the render commit of TransferStep2 when its deps shift after the success→auction navigation. E2E confirmed: login → /transfer/new (SN, 100 EUR, cash, Mariam Diallo) → details (fee 2%) → recap → PIN 123456 → success page renders correctly with 10-digit code 4955265114 + QR placeholder. Tap 'Voir les enchères' → bounce to /transfer/new. No LIVE badge, no 'Tour 1/5' timer card, no auction WebSocket snapshot.

ui_bugs.issue: STRUCTURAL: lines 29-38 — `if (!draft) return null;` is placed BEFORE `useEffect(() => { if (!draft) router.replace('/transfer/new'); }, [draft, router]);`. The eslint-disable-next-line bypasses Rules-of-Hooks but does not fix the actual hook-list mismatch. Result: when details.tsx is still mounted under success/auction in the Expo Router web stack and re-renders due to upstream state changes (patchDraft from recap.tsx adds a `result` field to draft, and/or the `router` reference changes after success.goNext's router.replace), the registered effect synchronously fires router.replace('/transfer/new') from inside a render phase. React's red console message confirms this exact pattern: setState (navigation) happening inside another component's render. Removing clearDraft from success.tsx did NOT eliminate the trigger — `router` reference change alone is enough to re-run the effect, and any rerender-time path inside details.tsx during the auction transition still calls navigation.

Same effect-pattern at lines 25-29 (useEffect → if (!draft) router.replace('/transfer/new')) is also vulnerable when the screen remains mounted under success during the success→auction transition. recap.tsx places the effect ABOVE the early return so it does not violate Rules-of-Hooks, but it still has no guard against post-confirmation re-runs. Less likely than details.tsx to fire here because recap.tsx unmounts when recap.replace('/transfer/success') executes; included for completeness.

integration_issues.issue: 100% reproducible bounce to /transfer/new. Auction screen never mounts, no bids fetched, no WS connection, no LIVE badge. Same as iter_5 and iter_6. clearDraft removal was a false-trail fix; the actual root cause is in details.tsx's render-phase navigation.

react_native_issues.issue: Rules-of-Hooks violation silenced with `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` at line 35. This is a code smell flagged in iteration_6 that has NOT been addressed. The disable should be removed, the useEffect moved ABOVE the early return, and a ref-guard added to prevent post-success re-redirects.

action_items: APPLY THE SAME PATTERN to recap.tsx (defensive — current symptoms point at details.tsx but recap has the same shape).

Re-run the same E2E to verify: login client@sendbid.app/Client@123! → /transfer/new (SN 100 EUR cash Mariam Diallo) → details (fee 2%) → recap → confirm-pin-submit (PIN 123456) → success → tap success-continue → MUST land and STAY on /transfer/auction with LIVE badge + 90s timer + WebSocket snapshot.
critical_code_review_comments: details.tsx:35 — `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` is the canonical sign of the bug. Linting rules exist to catch exactly this class of issue: a useEffect placed after a conditional early return runs against an inconsistent hook list. Silencing the lint does not silence the React runtime, which explains why the console error (`Cannot update a component while rendering a different component`) reappears identically across 3 fix attempts.

Three iterations (5, 6, 7) of fixes have targeted the SYMPTOM (clearDraft, setTimeout, useEffect) without removing this eslint-disable + early-return-before-hook combo. The eslint-disable should be treated as a P0 to be removed, not an accepted permanent waiver.

GENERAL: in Expo Router web stacks, screens earlier in the stack are NOT immediately unmounted on forward navigation. They re-render in response to global state (Zustand) for several frames. Any redirect-on-falsy-state useEffect in those screens MUST distinguish 'mounted-without-state' from 'state-just-cleared-after-I-did-my-job' using a ref or sentinel, otherwise it will fight legitimate forward navigations.

rca_of_issue: REPRODUCTION (100%, this iter; 3/3 across iterations 5+6+7): tap success-continue → URL = /transfer/new within ~300 ms and remains there through T+8000ms. Console: 'Cannot update a component (ForwardRef(NavigationContainerInner)) while rendering a different component (TransferStep2 ./transfer/details.tsx)'. CORRECTED MECHANISM (revised vs iter_6): clearDraft is now NEVER called, yet the bug persists. Therefore the trigger is NOT a draft→null transition. The trigger is the `router` reference changing inside details.tsx (still mounted in the Expo Router web stack under success→auction) which re-runs its `useEffect(..., [draft, router])`. Because details.tsx places that useEffect AFTER `if (!draft) return null` (line 29) with an eslint-disable to bypass the Rules-of-Hooks violation, React's effect machinery is misaligned: when the effect re-runs in a render commit triggered by the upstream router transition, its setState (router.replace('/transfer/new')) executes inside the render phase of TransferStep2 itself — which is exactly the error message React prints. Even if `if (!draft)` is logically false at this moment, the very fact that the effect runs synchronously inside another component's render is enough to either (a) actually call router.replace because of an intermediate render where draft was momentarily falsy, or (b) interfere with the just-issued router.replace('/transfer/auction'), causing Expo Router's web URL resolver to fall back to /transfer/new. MITIGATION: see action_items #1 — declare ALL hooks at the top of the function (no early return between hooks), remove the eslint-disable, and add a hadDraftRef sentinel so the redirect only fires on true cold-mount (deep-link / refresh), never post-confirmation. clearDraft can stay removed (defensive), but the structural hook fix is what actually resolves this bug class.
